newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end higher, led by Bavaria.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end higher, led by Bavaria.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended higher in active trading led by brewing giant Bavaria, flagship of the Julio Mario Santo Domingo conglomerate.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index closed up 0.39 percent at 17,038.17 on volume of more than 1.9 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB ended up 0.61 percent, meanwhile, closing at 1,112.06 on above-average volume of about 2.1 billion pesos.

Bavaria, the country's hottest stock, accounted for two billion pesos of volume. It rose 1.91 percent in Bogota to a new all-time high of 8,001 pesos per share on continuing buying after its announcement of an imminent share split.
Brokers said buying was also fueled by market rumors that a stake in Bavaria might be sold to Brazilian brewer Brahma. Bavaria could not be reached for comment on the rumors.
Other gainers, as stocks closed higher for the sixth consecutive trading session, included banks and cement companies.
Banco de Bogota closed up 1.54 percent in both Bogota and Medellin at 6,250 pesos per share.
Traders said the speculative move up appeared driven by the bank's relatively low market valuation since there was no news to explain the upward trend.
Banco Ganadero and Banco Industrial Colombiano also posted modest gains on what brokers described as a favorable reception to recent moves to slash their past-due loan portfolios.

Cementos del Caribe, which closed up 3.72 in Bogota Monday, extended its gains by rising another 1.49 percent to close at 5,685 pesos per share on what traders described as continuing buying by foreign funds. The tightly run cement company belongs to the highly diversified Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate, long considered one the darlings of foreign funds operating in Colombia.
